entries: Ionic bonding: sodium gives an electron away - sodium (2,8,1) transfers its lone outer electron to chlorine (2,8,7), forming a positive sodium ion and a negative chloride ion that attract each other.
slots.label: Ionic bonding
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The ionic lattice - the ions pack into one giant repeating lattice, every sodium ion surrounded by chloride ions; NaCl is the 1 to 1 ratio, not a molecule.
slots.label: The ionic lattice
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Covalent bonding: sharing, not giving - two chlorine atoms each contribute one electron to a shared pair, so both count eight outer electrons and form a molecule.
slots.label: Covalent bonding
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Metallic bonding: a sea of electrons - metal atoms release their outer electrons into a free-moving sea around a lattice of positive ions, which is why metals conduct and bend.
slots.label: Metallic bonding
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Check the thinking - a tidy formula does not mean a molecule: ask what the outer electrons do - transferred is ionic, shared is covalent, pooled is metallic.
slots.label: Check the thinking
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A charged particle formed when an atom loses electrons (positive ion) or gains electrons (negative ion).
slots.label: Ion
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed when one atom transfers outer electrons to another.
slots.label: Ionic bond
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A giant regular repeating pattern of particles. In an ionic compound every ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions, with no separate molecules.
slots.label: Lattice
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A bond formed when two atoms share a pair of electrons, each atom counting the shared pair in its outer shell.
slots.label: Covalent bond
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A small separate particle of joined atoms held by covalent bonds, such as a water molecule. Ionic compounds do not form molecules.
slots.label: Molecule
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The attraction between a lattice of positive metal ions and the sea of free electrons moving around them.
slots.label: Metallic bond
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Outer electrons that have left their own atoms and are free to move through a whole structure, as in a metal.
slots.label: Delocalised electrons
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The pull between opposite charges. It holds ions together in an ionic lattice and holds metal ions in their electron sea.
slots.label: Electrostatic attraction
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
